{"mode":"iff","restated":"∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ r < 1 ∧ ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, v n ≤ C * r ^ n","proof":"unfold QuantumParallelRepetition.HasExponentialBound
have key : ∀ (t : ℝ) (n : ℕ), Real.exp (t * (n : ℝ)) = Real.exp t ^ n := by
  intro t n
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ k ih => rw [Nat.cast_succ, mul_add, mul_one, Real.exp_add, ih, pow_succ]
constructor
· rintro ⟨c, hc, C, hC, h⟩
  refine ⟨Real.exp (-c), Real.exp_pos _, Real.exp_lt_one (by linarith), C, hC, fun n => ?_⟩
  have h1 := h n
  rw [key (-c) n] at h1
  exact h1
· rintro ⟨r, hr0, hr1, C, hC, h⟩
  refine ⟨-Real.log r, ?_, C, hC, fun n => ?_⟩
  · have h2 := Real.log_lt_log hr0 hr1
    rw [Real.log_one] at h2
    linarith
  · have e : Real.exp (-(-Real.log r) * (n : ℝ)) = r ^ n := by
      rw [neg_neg, key, Real.exp_log hr0]
    rw [e]
    exact h n","english":"There exist a ratio r with 0 < r < 1 and a constant C > 0 such that v n ≤ C · rⁿ for every natural number n.","why_clearer":"It replaces the exponential exp(-c·n) by an ordinary geometric decay rate r = e^{-c} ∈ (0,1), the standard way to say 'exponentially decaying bound'."}

parsed.restated: ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ r < 1 ∧ ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, v n ≤ C * r ^ n
parsed.proof:
unfold QuantumParallelRepetition.HasExponentialBound
have key : ∀ (t : ℝ) (n : ℕ), Real.exp (t * (n : ℝ)) = Real.exp t ^ n := by
  intro t n
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ k ih => rw [Nat.cast_succ, mul_add, mul_one, Real.exp_add, ih, pow_succ]
constructor
· rintro ⟨c, hc, C, hC, h⟩
  refine ⟨Real.exp (-c), Real.exp_pos _, Real.exp_lt_one (by linarith), C, hC, fun n => ?_⟩
  have h1 := h n
  rw [key (-c) n] at h1
  exact h1
· rintro ⟨r, hr0, hr1, C, hC, h⟩
  refine ⟨-Real.log r, ?_, C, hC, fun n => ?_⟩
  · have h2 := Real.log_lt_log hr0 hr1
    rw [Real.log_one] at h2
    linarith
  · have e : Real.exp (-(-Real.log r) * (n : ℝ)) = r ^ n := by
      rw [neg_neg, key, Real.exp_log hr0]
    rw [e]
    exact h n
parsed.english: There exist a ratio r with 0 < r < 1 and a constant C > 0 such that v n ≤ C · rⁿ for every natural number n.
parsed.why_clearer: It replaces the exponential exp(-c·n) by an ordinary geometric decay rate r = e^{-c} ∈ (0,1), the standard way to say 'exponentially decaying bound'.
